summary: Right-handed volleyball spike, final plant of the approach: both feet planted, knees deeply bent, both arms swung far back, just before the jump.

environment.text: Net: top tape 2.43 m high, {fwd:net_top:pelvis} cm in front of the hips; the set ball is still rising toward the attack point above and in front.

cameras.name: side_low
cameras.text: Sharp focus on the planted feet and the swung-back arms, shallow depth of field.

cameras.name: front_three_quarter
cameras.text: Knees and arms read clearly, net tape out of frame above.

cameras.name: wide_cinema
cameras.text: Wide cinematic frame from behind the attacker, court lines leading to the net.

rules.why: dominant knee about 90 deg flexion at the deepest plant (elite males 90, females 84)
arms at maximum backswing, shoulders hyperextended (extension limit about 60 deg)
arms swung behind the body, not to the side

text.action: a volleyball attacker on the last plant step of the spike approach, just before jumping
text.core: Both feet planted flat, left foot slightly ahead; right knee bent to about 90 degrees, left knee about 65 degrees; trunk leaning about 38 degrees forward; both arms swung straight back behind the hips, palms facing back, at the end of the backswing; eyes up on the set ball.
text.gaze: Eyes up on the incoming set above the net.
cues: wide, dynamic arm swing loads the jump
plant heel-to-toe with the feet ahead of the hips so the body leans back into the jump
kinetic: motion blur on both arms at the end of the backswing
shoe soles gripping the court, slight squeak dust at the heels
jersey pulled back by the arm swing

sources.cite: Fuchs et al. 2019, J Sports Sci 37(21): spike jump plant angles, torso incline, jump height of elite players (search extract)
Wagner et al. 2009, Int J Sports Med: arm backswing (shoulder hyperextension velocity) predicts jump height
Fuchs et al. 2019, J Sci Med Sport: wide dynamic arm swing in the approach
